name: Garden of the Sleeping Giant
note: Garden: former private orchid nursery of Raymond Burr with hilly walking paths and tropical plantings; entry charged. Inside the span of Nadi and reached from that base.

name: Sri Siva Subramaniya Temple
note: Religious site: large Dravidian-style Hindu temple at the southern end of Nadi; visitors cover up and enter the interior, free to enter. Inside the span of Nadi and reached from that base.

name: Sabeto Hot Springs and Mud Pool
note: Natural attraction: mud bath and three hot-spring pools in the Sabeto valley near Nadi; mud treatments and massages offered. Inside the span of Nadi and reached from that base.

name: Koroyanitu National Heritage Park
note: Park: 35 km2 heritage park around Mount Koroyanitu behind Lautoka and Nadi, with walking trails from Abaca village. Inside the span of Nadi and reached from that base.

name: Viseisei Village
note: Village: the oldest settlement in Fiji, said to be where the first Melanesian canoes beached at nearby Vuda Point; a $5 entry fee applies. Inside the span of Nadi and reached from that base.

name: Wailoaloa Beach
note: Beach: 3 km sand beach north of Nadi town, lined with resorts and beach clubs; a swimming and sunset spot. Inside the span of Nadi and reached from that base.

name: Nadi Produce Market
note: Market: daily fresh produce market on Hospital Road, Nadi, open Monday to Saturday. Inside the span of Nadi and reached from that base.

name: Nausori Highlands
note: Highlands: dry-zone mountain rainforest behind Nadi offering nature walks, hikes and off-road tours. Kept in west region, also a review in central: one spot only.

name: Lautoka Market
note: Market: large covered produce, spice and kava market beside the Lautoka bus station. Represents Lautoka (kept as a town: folded into this market spot and the Nadi description, not listed beside its own market).

name: Monuriki
note: Uninhabited island: the Cast Away filming island (2000 film), with white beaches and a pine forest; Wikivoyage calls it very much off the beaten track. Inside the span of Mamanuca Islands and reached from that base.

name: Mana Island
note: Island resort: three beach areas, lagoon snorkelling and water sports; a Survivor filming location. Inside the span of Mamanuca Islands and reached from that base.

name: Beachcomber Island
note: Island resort: a private island with a backpacker resort, snorkelling, dive shop and the nightly Bula Dance; reached from Denarau by catamaran. Inside the span of Mamanuca Islands and reached from that base.

name: Treasure Island
note: Island resort: a marine reserve island with palm beaches, snorkelling, a turtle restoration programme and family facilities. Inside the span of Mamanuca Islands and reached from that base.

name: South Sea Island
note: Island resort: a 30-minute day trip from Denarau with a pool, snorkel gear, kayaks and a semi-submersible coral viewer. Inside the span of Mamanuca Islands and reached from that base.

name: Bounty Island
note: Island: a marine-reserve island (Bounty Island, Kadavulailai) with white beaches, a small resort and snorkelling. Inside the span of Mamanuca Islands and reached from that base.

name: Cloudbreak
note: Surf break: the headline reef wave off Tavarua, a world-class right in the southern Mamanucas (no article of its own; Wikipedia Cloudbreak redirects to Tavarua). Inside the span of Mamanuca Islands and reached from that base.

name: Sawa-i-Lau Caves
note: Cave: limestone sea caves on Sawa-i-Lau islet off the southern tip of Yasawa Island, swum into by boat trip (one reached by an underwater passage, daylight in the largest cave); the cave trip Wikivoyage lists under Do. Tourism board page seen in search only (fetch blocked). Inside the span of Yasawa Islands and reached from that base.

name: Blue Lagoon
note: Beach and snorkel lagoon on the west side of Nanuya Lailai, the film location of The Blue Lagoon (1980); a fish sanctuary with coral, reached on Blue Lagoon Cruises day trips. Wikivoyage: the real Blue Lagoon is privately owned, this is the day-trip beach. No article under this name (the title is a disambiguation page), so views are 0 and a disambiguated wiki title is still needed. Inside the span of Yasawa Islands and reached from that base.

name: Nanuya Lailai
note: Island: next to the Blue Lagoon and Turtle Island; Wikivoyage lists a walk over the island with views, the Blue Lagoon snorkel and diving from its dive shop. Inside the span of Yasawa Islands and reached from that base.

name: Waya Lailai
note: Island: also called Wayasewa, with a rocky volcanic peak at its centre; Wikivoyage recommends the climb to the top for sunrise, and a three-hour walk across the island to Naboro village. Inside the span of Yasawa Islands and reached from that base.

name: Sigatoka Sand Dunes National Park
note: National park: Fiji's first national park, 20–60 m parabolic dunes at the Sigatoka River mouth with archaeological sites. Inside the span of Coral Coast and reached from that base.

name: Natadola Beach
note: Beach: white-sand beach west of Sigatoka, considered one of the best in Fiji, with shade trees and horse riding. Inside the span of Coral Coast and reached from that base.

name: Beqa Island
note: island: lagoon island 10 km off Viti Levu, base for shark dives and firewalking villages, reached by boat from Pacific Harbour Inside the span of Coral Coast and reached from that base. (spot comes from region fiji-kadavu)

name: Beqa Shark Reef
note: Dive site: Shark Reef marine park in the Beqa lagoon, dived from Pacific Harbour with shark-dive operators; the place, not an operator. Merged with kadavu-region "Shark Reef (Beqa Lagoon)" (same dive site; run from Pacific Harbour). (spot comes from region fiji-viti-levu-central)

name: Navua River
note: River: Upper Navua Gorge whitewater rafting through black volcanic canyon and waterfalls, reached by road from Navua. Inside the span of Coral Coast and reached from that base. (spot comes from region fiji-viti-levu-central)

name: Biausevu Waterfalls
note: Waterfall: 20 m tiered waterfall reached by a 20-minute rainforest walk near Biausevu, best just after the wet season. Inside the span of Coral Coast and reached from that base.

name: Tavuni Hill Fort
note: Historic site: semi-restored 18th-century hill fort near Naroro village, with guides on precolonial history. Inside the span of Coral Coast and reached from that base.

name: Kula Eco Park
note: Wildlife park: captive breeding of endangered species and environmental education, Pacific Harbour side; paid entry (east of Sigatoka, check central region). Merged with the central-region entry "Kula WILD Adventure Park" (same place, Sigatoka).

name: Nananu-i-Ra
note: Island: small island off Rakiraki reached by boat from Ellington Wharf, with resorts, the One Bay beach and famous dive sites. Inside the span of Rakiraki and reached from that base.

name: One Bay Beach
note: Beach: white sand beach on Nananu-i-Ra with a rainforest behind and an ancient village; a sunset and swimming beach. Inside the span of Rakiraki and reached from that base.

name: Ratu Udre Udre Tomb
note: Historic site: tomb of 19th-century chief Udre Udre, said to have eaten hundreds of people, near Vaileka. Inside the span of Rakiraki and reached from that base.

name: Navatu Rock
note: Landmark: rock beside Kings Road in Vitawa village that looks like a man or a woman depending on the angle; one of Fiji's oldest settlement sites. Inside the span of Rakiraki and reached from that base.

name: Fiji Museum
note: Museum: national museum of Fiji's history and archaeology (artefacts about 3,700 years old), in Thurston Gardens, Suva; paid entry. Inside the span of Suva and reached from that base.

name: Colo-i-Suva Forest Reserve
note: Nature park: rainforest reserve about 10 minutes from central Suva, with Waisila Falls, swimming pools, trails and birdlife. Inside the span of Suva and reached from that base.

name: Suva Municipal Market
note: Market: daily fruit and vegetable market on Harris Road, Suva (Mon-Sat), south of the bus station. Inside the span of Suva and reached from that base.

name: Mount Korobaba
note: Viewpoint: hill walk above Lami with city and harbour views; the walk starts behind the cement works in Lami. Inside the span of Suva and reached from that base.

name: 199 Steps (Mission Hill)
note: walk: about 199 steps up Mission Hill above Levuka to old Methodist mission buildings and a panorama over the offshore islands and Lekaleka Reef (Wikivoyage Levuka: walk up the 199 steps). Inside the span of Levuka and reached from that base.

name: Levuka Community Centre and Museum
note: museum: restored 1878 Morris Hedstrom trading store housing a branch of the Fiji Museum, a library and the Levuka town museum; walking tours start here (Wikipedia Levuka; Wikivoyage Levuka suggests the town museum). Inside the span of Levuka and reached from that base.

name: Ovalau Peak
note: viewpoint: hike to the mountain peak above Levuka, overlooking the reefs and the Koro Sea (Wikivoyage Levuka 'See' lists the hike). Coordinates unresolved: no OSM natural=peak found; the Ovalau article point is the island centre, not the peak. Inside the span of Levuka and reached from that base.

name: Lovoni
note: village: traditional village in the fertile crater of Ovalau, reached by guided tour on foot and by truck; visitors take a village tour and lunch (Wikivoyage Ovalau, Levuka). Inside the span of Levuka and reached from that base.

name: Leleuvia
note: island: coral cay about 45 minutes by boat from Levuka with day trips and simple overnight bures (Wikivoyage Ovalau, Levuka). Inside the span of Levuka and reached from that base.

name: Caqalai
note: island: coral island run by the Methodist Church with simple bures, white sand beaches and snorkelling; day trips from Levuka (Wikivoyage Levuka). Inside the span of Levuka and reached from that base.

name: Tavoro Waterfalls
note: Waterfalls (nature): three falls in Bouma park, the most accessible on Taveuni, 15 minutes to an hour's walk. Inside the span of Taveuni and reached from that base.

name: Lavena Coastal Walk
note: Walk (coastal track): about four hours return from Lavena village to a swimming hole and waterfalls, with a small fee. Inside the span of Taveuni and reached from that base.

name: Des Voeux Peak
note: Peak (mountain): Fiji's second-highest peak at 1,196 m, reached by hike or 4WD, with birdlife. Inside the span of Taveuni and reached from that base.

name: Rainbow Reef
note: Reef (dive area): patch reef in the Somosomo Strait between Taveuni and Vanua Levu, one of the South Pacific's best-known dive sites. Inside the span of Taveuni and reached from that base.

name: Waitabu Marine Park
note: Marine park (community reef): 1 km of fringing reef protected by seven communities, with snorkelling. Inside the span of Taveuni and reached from that base.

name: Lake Tagimaucia
note: Lake (crater lake): volcanic crater lake at about 800 m, habitat of the tagimaucia flower, reached by guided hike. Inside the span of Taveuni and reached from that base.

name: Beverley Beach
note: White-sand beach at Matei on Taveuni, named by Rough Guides for snorkelling. Inside the span of Taveuni and reached from that base.

name: Vidawa Rainforest Hike
note: Walk (guided rainforest hike): full-day guided hike to archaeological sites and viewpoints, ending at the lower Tavoro falls. Inside the span of Taveuni and reached from that base.

name: Waitavala Waterslide
note: Waterslide (natural rock slide): cool natural rock slide and swimming hole on a stream. Inside the span of Taveuni and reached from that base.

name: Wairiki Mission Church
note: Religious building (mission church): Taveuni Catholic church on a hill above a coconut plantation, with views of the historic battle beach. Inside the span of Taveuni and reached from that base.

name: Savusavu
note: Town on Vanua Levu's south coast: yachting anchorage, diving base and hot springs, the island's main tourist centre. Town with hot springs, anchorage and diving base; has draws no other spot covers.

name: Waisali Rainforest Reserve
note: Protected rainforest reserve (nature park) just outside Savusavu, about 130 ha, with birds, frogs and a waterfall walk; run with the National Trust of Fiji. Inside the span of Vanua Levu and reached from that base.

name: Labasa
note: Town: largest town on Vanua Levu and its administrative and sugar centre, with a bus hub and Indo-Fijian market life. Largest Vanua Levu town and bus hub; its market and temple are only review candidates, so the town itself is the spot.

name: Savusavu Hills
note: Walk (hike): hill ridge above Savusavu with bay views, 30 minutes to a few hours by route. Inside the span of Vanua Levu and reached from that base.

name: Lesiaceva Point
note: Headland (viewpoint and beach): south coast point near Savusavu, with a public snorkelling beach at Split Rock. Inside the span of Vanua Levu and reached from that base.

name: Kadavu Island
note: island: the base for the whole Kadavu group, a destination rather than a spot Kadavu has only three other kept places (Great Astrolabe Reef, Nabukelevu, Kavala Bay Waterfall): below the four-spot bar, so the island is a standalone island spot (like Kapiti Island) and its three draws stand alone beside it. Owner: if the 10 review candidates (Naiqoro Passage, Namalata Bay, Soso Passage, beaches...) are approved, promote Kadavu to a destination.

name: Great Astrolabe Reef
note: reef: barrier reef with 60+ dive and snorkel sites, the island's principal draw Barrier reef with 60+ dive/snorkel sites off Kadavu; reached by boat from Kadavu resorts; no destination within reach.

name: Kavala Bay Waterfall
note: waterfall: 45-minute climb to a high waterfall with a swimming hole, reached by boat through mangroves at high tide 45-minute climb reached by boat on Kadavu; no destination within reach.

name: Nabukelevu
note: mountain: 805 m inactive volcano and highest point of Kadavu, known as Mount Washington Mount Washington, Kadavu high point; no destination within reach.

name: Navala Village
note: Village: traditional bure village inland from Ba, where visitors stay in basic homestays; the source is Wikipedia only, a tourism source still needed. Traditional bure village inland from Ba; reached by the Nadi-Ba-Navala road/day tours, outside the Nadi span (about 55 km) and over 40 km from Rakiraki.

name: Mount Tomanivi
note: Peak: Fiji's highest point (1,324 m) in the interior of Viti Levu; a climb rather than a managed attraction, no visitor source checked yet. Coordinates lie in the north-west highlands; check which region judges it. Fiji highest peak, interior Viti Levu, climbed from Nadarivatu/Navala side. About 34 km from Rakiraki centre but outside its 30 km reach (span 40) and not reached from the Suncoast base.

name: Vanua Balavu
note: Island in the northern Lau Group, one of the two main visitor islands with homestays, a guesthouse, Lomaloma port and the Bay of Islands; reached by domestic flight or charter. Northern Lau island, homestay-based; Lau has no other destination (remote, flights/ferries).

name: Bay of Islands, Vanua Balavu
note: Natural bay of islets and a limestone cathedral cave with snorkelling, on the northern tip of Vanua Balavu; Wikipedia's Vanua Balavu article gives its other name as Qilaqila, a marine reserve (permission to anchor needed). Reached by yacht, seaplane or charter. Limestone islets and Cathedral Cave on Vanua Balavu; pinned apart from the island. Lau stays standalone (three kept places on different islands).

name: Lakeba
note: Island in the southern Lau Group, the administrative and population centre with a weekly flight, homestays and caves, hillforts and Tongan-influenced villages; reached by air or boat. Southern Lau island; no destination within reach.

name: Losa Beach
note: Beach: one of the best beaches on Rotuma, west of Solroroa Bluff (Wikivoyage Do). Village of Losa is in Ituʻtiʻu district. Rotuma beach; three kept places (below the four-spot bar), Rotuma is remote.

name: Vai'oa Beach
note: Beach: one of the best beaches on Rotuma, west of Solroroa Bluff (Wikivoyage Do). No article. Rotuma beach, as above.

name: Oinafa Beach
note: Beach: one of the best beaches on Rotuma, in the Oinafa district on the east (Wikivoyage Do). Wiki title is the district article, so views are 0. No beach point found: the district article point is not used. Rotuma beach, as above.
